phase: Optional claim corrections, Lite LOW. Numeric-zero filtering defect exists, but retained preconditions focus on harmless False defaults. Verifier did not adequately narrow the text. Owner inspection is necessary.

verification_decisions.reason: The dictionary comprehension uses `if v` to filter values, which drops explicit `False` or falsy configuration values like `0`, causing them to incorrectly fall back to dataclass defaults.

findings.title: Boolean and falsey configuration values filtered out by `if v` check
findings.impact: Boolean flags such as `include_source_str` or `ask_for_clarification` set to `False` (or any `0`/empty values) will be filtered out by `if v`, causing them to incorrectly fall back to dataclass default values instead of respecting explicit `False` settings from environment variables or `configurable`.
findings.preconditions: A user sets `include_source_str = False` or `ask_for_clarification = False` in `configurable` or via environment variables.
findings.explanation: Line 67 filters out any value where `v` is falsy (`if {k: v for k, v in values.items() if v}`). Since `False` is falsy in Python, explicit `False` settings are discarded.
findings.suggestion: return cls(**{k: v for k, v in values.items() if v is not None})
